latest_release.name: Spec Kit - 1.4.0
latest_release.body:
## Install

```bash
uv tool install specify-cli --from git+https://github.com/github/spec-kit.git@v1.4.0
specify init my-project
```

## What's Changed

- chore: bump version to 1.4.0
- Use handle-based reads in FileHelper (#5351)
- chore: limit automatic Python 3.11 tests to Linux (#5367)
- Harden initial URL validation in HTTP helpers (#5350)
- Update SpecKit Companion extension to v0.26.0 (#5365)
- Use handle-based text overwrites in FileHelper (#5353)
- Require HTTPS consistently for catalog sources (#5355)
- feat(workflows): workflow functions - project-installed custom pipe filters (#5303)
- feat(integrations): map reasoning effort and context size for Copilot, Codex, and Claude Code (#5249)
- [bundle] Update Spec Kit for Azure DevOps bundle to v0.3.2 (#5346)
- [extension] Add T-Shirt Sizing Gate extension to community catalog (#5332)
- fix(scripts): treat option-like feature descriptions as text in create-new-feature.sh (#5245)
- fix(self-upgrade): don't offer a .dev0/.post0 build's base tag as the rollback version (#5358)
- fix: preserve existing priority from registry when installing/refreshing bundles (#5331)
- test(workflows): pin numeric equality on captured shell stdout with trailing newline (#5357)
- fix(extensions): show catalog entries missing name, version or description (#5308)
- Use handle-based exclusive creation in FileHelper (#5354)
- Validate release tags before running release steps (#5356)
- feat(omp): support integration args and options in build_exec_args (#4876)
- Add Spec Kit for Azure DevOps — human-gated lifecycle extension to community catalog (#5348)
- chore: release 1.3.3, begin 1.3.4.dev0 development (#5349)

detail.readme:
🌱 Spec Kit

Build with a spec, fix a bug, or assess an idea — with your coding agent.

English · 简体中文 · 日本語 · 한국어

Spec Kit is an open source toolkit that gives AI coding agents structured processes, reusable templates, and documented outcomes. Start with a ready-made process, customize it, or bring your own. ## Choose your process | What you need | Process | Outcome | | --- | --- | --- | | Build a feature or application | [Spec-Driven Development](#spec-driven-development) | A specification carried through planning, implementation, and convergence | | Diagnose and repair broken behavior | [Bug fixing](#bug-fixing) | An assessed cause, scoped fix, and recorded verification | | Decide whether an idea deserves investment | [Idea assessment](#idea-assessment) | An evidence-backed go, clarify, or stop decision | | Adopt or create a different process | [Your own process](#capabilities) | A process adapted or assembled from reusable primitives | These are independent entry points, not mandatory phases. SDD ships in core; bug fixing and assessment are bundled extensions you install when needed, and the primitives below let you adopt or create other processes. ## Capabilities Spec Kit combines ready-to-use processes with composable mechanisms: | Capability | Spec Kit mechanism | | --- | --- | | Connect to or switch between coding agents | [Integration](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/integrations/index.html) | | Add a command, quality gate, or complete process | [Extension](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/extensions/overview.html) | | Connect a process to an external tool or service | [Extension](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/extensions/overview.html) | | React to coding-agent lifecycle events | [Extension runtime event](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/extensions/api.html#extension-runtime-events) | | Run extension commands before or after Spec Kit commands | [Extension hook](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/extensions/api.html#hook-configuration) | | Adapt templates, commands, terminology, or methodology | [Preset](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/presets/overview.html) | | Enforce organizational or regulatory standards | [Preset](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/presets/overview.html) | | Override a template for one project | [Project-local override](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/how-to/customization.html#project-local-overrides-and-resolution) | | Automate prompts, commands, gates, and shell tasks | [Workflow](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/workflows/overview.html) | | Modify an installed workflow without forking it | [Workflow overlay](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/workflows/overlays.html) | | Add reusable executable behavior to workflows | [Workflow step](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/workflow-steps/developing.html#custom-step-packages) | | Install a curated setup for a role or team | [Bundle](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/bundles/overview.html) | | Discover community components | [Catalog](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/overview/catalogs.html) | | Host a private catalog of approved components | [Catalog](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/overview/catalogs.html) | | Access private catalogs and component downloads | [Authentication](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/reference/authentication.html) | | Work offline or behind a firewall | [Local sources and self-hosted catalogs](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/install/air-gapped.html) | | Inspect which layer supplies a command, template, or script | [Artifact inventory](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/overview/artifacts.html) | Search the active catalogs with commands such as `specify extension search`, `specify preset search`, `specify workflow search`, and `specify bundle search`. Spec Kit includes community catalogs, and organizations can add their own curated sources. Catalog listings are not audits or endorsements, so review community source code before installing or running it. ## Get started You need Python 3.11+, [uv](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/install/uv.html), and a supported AI coding agent on Linux, macOS, or Windows. Run these commands in your terminal to install Spec Kit and create a project. This example uses GitHub Copilot. ```bash uv tool install specify-cli specify init my-project --integration copilot cd my-project ``` After installing the Specify CLI and creating your project, launch your coding agent in the project directory, then choose a process below. For other setups: - [Installation](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/installation.html) for pinned releases, other installers, CI, and troubleshooting. - [Existing projects](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/how-to/existing-projects.html) to start with code you already have. - [Other agents](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/integrations/index.html) for integration keys and [invocation syntax](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/integrations/cli.html#command-invocation). - [Upgrade](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/upgrade.html) to update an existing installation. ## Spec-Driven Development Define what to build and why, then turn the specification into a plan, tasks, and working code. The minimal flow is shown below. Create a constitution once per project and repeat the remaining steps for each feature. Run these skills in your agent's chat, not your terminal, one at a time, reviewing each result before continuing. This example uses GitHub Copilot's default skills syntax. For another agent, use its [equivalent invocation syntax](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/integrations/cli.html#command-invocation). ```text /speckit-constitution Create principles focused on code quality, testing, and maintainability. /speckit-specify Build a photo organizer with albums grouped by date and a tile preview of each album. /speckit-plan Use Vite with vanilla JavaScript. Keep images local and store metadata in SQLite. /speckit-tasks /speckit-implement /speckit-converge ``` Repeat implement and converge until convergence reports `Converged`. For clarification, checklists, and consistency analysis, see the SDD walkthrough. [SDD walkthrough](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/quickstart.html) · [Command reference](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/reference/agentic-sdd.html) ## Bug fixing Assess the cause, fix the bug, and verify the original symptom is resolved. No SDD feature workflow is required first. Install the bug-fixing extension in your terminal, from the project directory: ```bash specify extension add bug ``` Run these skills in your agent's chat, not your terminal, one at a time, reviewing each result before continuing. This example uses GitHub Copilot's default skills syntax. For another agent, use its [equivalent invocation syntax](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/integrations/cli.html#command-invocation). ```text /speckit-bug-assess "Submitting an empty password crashes the login form." slug=login-crash /speckit-bug-fix slug=login-crash /speckit-bug-test slug=login-crash ``` Review the reports in `.specify/bugs/login-crash/`. The final verdict is `verified`, `partial`, or `failed`; only `verified` confirms a successful fix. [Bug-fixing walkthrough](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/guides/bugfix.html) · [Command reference](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/reference/agentic-bugfix.html) ## Idea assessment Gather evidence to decide whether an idea is worth pursuing. No source code or SDD feature workflow is required. Install the assessment extension in your terminal, from the project directory: ```bash specify extension add assess ``` Run these skills in your agent's chat, not your terminal, one at a time, reviewing each result before continuing. This example uses GitHub Copilot's default skills syntax. For another agent, use its [equivalent invocation syntax](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/integrations/cli.html#command-invocation). ```text /speckit-assess-intake "Let users work offline and sync when they reconnect." slug=offline-mode /speckit-assess-research slug=offline-mode /speckit-assess-define slug=offline-mode /speckit-assess-shape slug=offline-mode /speckit-assess-decide slug=offline-mode ``` Review the artifacts in `.specify/assessments/offline-mode/` and the final decision: `go`, `needs-clarification`, or `kill`. Resolve unknowns by editing the existing Markdown artifacts, directly or with your agent, rather than rerunning whole stages. If you choose to build a software idea with a `go` decision, establish a project constitution if needed, then pass the handoff summary from `decision.md` to `/speckit-specify`. Stopping with a documented reason is also a useful outcome. [Assessment walkthrough](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/guides/assessment.html) · [Command reference](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/reference/agentic-assessment.html) ## Customize or bring your own process Customize Spec-Driven Development, bug fixing, or idea assessment to fit your team's standards. Or bring your own process without adopting any of them. Combine the [capabilities above](#capabilities) to match your goal: - Adapt an existing process with a preset, such as requiring regulatory traceability in plans. Use a project-local override for a one-off template change. - Bring your own process by adding its commands through an extension and exposing them to your coding agent through an integration. - Automate commands and checks in a workflow. Use overlays to adapt an installed workflow without forking it, or add custom workflow steps when the built-in types are not enough. - Share a reusable setup by packaging its extensions, presets, workflows, and workflow steps in a bundle. Start with the smallest change that meets your needs; you do not have to replace the whole process. [Customization guide](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/how-to/customization.html) · [Community components and walkthroughs](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/community/overview.html) ## Documentation - [CLI reference](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/index.html#specify-cli) and [process commands](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/reference/agentic-sdd.html#command-overview) - [How-to guides](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/how-to/index.html) for applying Spec Kit to your project work - [SDD philosophy](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/how-to/sdd.html), [full methodology](./spec-driven.md), and [evolving existing specs](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/how-to/evolving-specs.html) - [Project history](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/overview/history.html) - [How Spec Kit uses Spec Kit](./CONTRIBUTING.md#does-spec-kit-use-spec-kit) ## In the news - [Open Source Friday: Spec Kit Part 2](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8hHCpNVLhmI) (October 16, 2026) — Manfred Riem and Nicole Haugen discuss Spec Kit 1.0 and the expanded toolkit. - [Living Specs in SpecKit](https://www.alfredo-perez.dev/blog/2026-10-15-living-specs) (October 15, 2026) — Alfredo Perez explores maintaining capability-level specifications as a project evolves. - [Spec Kit Customization Series](https://jesseliberty.com/2026/10/08/4-solutions-to-spec-kit-issues/) (October 8–10, 2026) — Jesse Liberty walks through presets and extension authoring, including testing and publishing. - [From Spec-First to Enterprise-Ready: Extending GitHub Spec Kit](https://developer.microsoft.com/blog/from-spec-first-to-enterprise-ready-extending-github-spec-kit/) (October 7, 2026) — Apoorv Gupta explains enterprise customization through presets, extensions, bundles, workflows, and governed catalogs. - [Open Source Friday with Spec Kit](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2IArMAhkJcE) (May 8, 2026) — An introduction and SDD demonstration with Manfred Riem. ## Star history

Thanks to everyone who helps Spec Kit shine.

## Support and contributing [Report a bug or request a feature](https://github.com/github/spec-kit/issues/new) · [Contributing guide](./CONTRIBUTING.md) · [Code of conduct](./CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) Spec Kit is [MIT licensed](./LICENSE).
detail.readme_zh:
🌱 Spec Kit

与你的编码助手一起，依据规范开发、修复缺陷，或评估想法。

English · 简体中文 · 日本語 · 한국어

Spec Kit 是一个开源工具套件，为 AI 编码助手提供结构化流程、可复用模板和有据可查的成果。 你可以从以下三种流程中任选一种开始，按需定制，也可以引入自己的流程。 ## 选择你的流程 | 你的需求 | 流程 | 产出 | | --- | --- | --- | | 构建功能或应用 | [规范驱动开发](#规范驱动开发) | 从规范出发，完成规划、实现与收敛 | | 排查并修复异常行为 | [缺陷修复](#缺陷修复) | 经评估的原因、范围明确的修复与验证记录 | | 判断一个想法是否值得投入 | [想法评估](#想法评估) | 基于证据决定推进、澄清或停止 | 这三种流程是**彼此独立的入口**，不是必须依次完成的三个阶段。 SDD 内置于核心；缺陷修复和想法评估由随工具提供的扩展实现，需要时再安装。 ## 快速开始 你需要 **Python 3.11+**、**[uv](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/install/uv.html)** 以及受支持的 AI 编码助手，可在 Linux、macOS 或 Windows 上使用。 **仅 CLI 配置步骤在终端中执行**：从 PyPI 安装 Spec Kit 并创建项目： ```bash uv tool install specify-cli specify init my-project --integration copilot cd my-project ``` CLI 只需安装一次，项目只需初始化一次；以下三种流程共用这套准备步骤。 示例采用 **GitHub Copilot 默认的技能（skills）模式**。 如需使用其他助手，将 `copilot` 替换为对应的 [集成标识](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/integrations/index.html)。 已有代码？请参阅[现有项目指南](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/how-to/existing-projects.html)。 锁定版本、其他安装方式、CI 与故障排查见[安装指南](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/installation.html)； 更新已安装的 CLI 和项目文件见[升级指南](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/upgrade.html)。 现在，在**项目目录中启动编码助手**，选择以下一种流程。 在**助手的聊天界面中逐个调用 `/speckit-*` 技能**，检查结果后再继续。 这些是助手技能，不是终端命令。其他助手或模式可能采用[不同的调用语法](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/integrations/cli.html#command-invocation)。 ## 规范驱动开发 先明确**做什么、为什么做**，再决定**怎么实现**。 规范驱动开发（SDD）将需求转化为规范、技术方案和可执行任务，再依据这些制品指导实现。 **每个项目先确立一次准则；每个功能依次完成：规范 → 方案 → 任务 → 实现 → 收敛。** 在助手的聊天界面中调用以下技能： ```text /speckit-constitution Create principles focused on code quality, testing, and maintainability. /speckit-specify Build a photo organizer with albums grouped by date and a tile preview of each album. /speckit-plan Use Vite with vanilla JavaScript. Keep images local and store metadata in SQLite. /speckit-tasks /speckit-implement /speckit-converge ``` 反复执行 **implement → converge**，直到收敛报告给出 **Converged**。 需要额外的质量把关时，可加入需求澄清、检查清单和一致性分析。 [SDD 实战指南](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/quickstart.html) · [命令参考](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/reference/agentic-sdd.html) ## 缺陷修复 将诊断、修复和验证分开，让助手针对评估出的原因修复，并检查最初出现的症状。 无需先走一遍 SDD 功能开发流程。 **CLI 配置（终端）**：在项目目录下安装这个可选扩展： ```bash specify extension add bug ``` 然后在助手的聊天界面中依次调用 **assess → fix → test**（评估 → 修复 → 测试）技能： ```text /speckit-bug-assess "Submitting an empty password crashes the login form." slug=login-crash /speckit-bug-fix slug=login-crash /speckit-bug-test slug=login-crash ``` 报告保存在 `.specify/bugs/login-crash/`。请检查最终结论： `verified`（已验证）、`partial`（部分验证）或 `failed`（失败）。缺少验证不算修复成功。 [缺陷修复指南](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/guides/bugfix.html) · [命令参考](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/reference/agentic-bugfix.html) ## 想法评估 在投入之前先收集证据，无论这个想法最终是否会成为软件。 这是一个独立流程，也适用于非软件类想法，即使项目中没有源代码也能使用。 **CLI 配置（终端）**：在项目目录下安装这个可选扩展： ```bash specify extension add assess ``` 然后在助手的聊天界面中依次调用 **intake → research → define → shape → decide** （收集想法 → 调研 → 定义问题 → 形成方案 → 决策）技能： ```text /speckit-assess-intake "Let users work offline and sync when they reconnect." slug=offline-mode /speckit-assess-research slug=offline-mode /speckit-assess-define slug=offline-mode /speckit-assess-shape slug=offline-mode /speckit-assess-decide slug=offline-mode ``` 制品保存在 `.specify/assessments/offline-mode/`，最终给出 **go / needs-clarification / kill**（推进 / 需要澄清 / 停止）的决策。 遇到待澄清问题时，直接完善已有的 Markdown 制品，或请助手协助修改，而不是重新生成整个阶段。 如果决定开发，可将 `go` 的评估结果交给 `/speckit-specify`；记录理由后停止，同样是有价值的结果。 [想法评估指南](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/guides/assessment.html) · [命令参考](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/reference/agentic-assessment.html) ## 定制或引入自己的流程 **扩展**新增能力，**预设**调整现有行为，**工作流**自动执行步骤，**捆绑包**打包面向角色的配置。 单个项目的一次性模板调整可使用项目本地覆盖；流程或术语的本地化可使用预设。 [定制指南](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/how-to/customization.html) · [社区扩展、预设、捆绑包与实战演练](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/community/overview.html) ## 文档 以下链接指向英文指南。工具升级与功能规范演进是两件事：升级时更新工具文件，需求变化时更新 `specs/` 制品。 - [CLI 参考](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/index.html#specify-cli)与[流程命令](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/reference/agentic-sdd.html#command-overview) - [SDD 理念](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/how-to/sdd.html)、[完整方法论](./spec-driven.md)与[现有规范演进](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/how-to/evolving-specs.html) - [项目历史](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/overview/history.html) - [Spec Kit 如何使用 Spec Kit](./CONTRIBUTING.md#does-spec-kit-use-spec-kit) ## 支持与贡献 [报告缺陷或提出功能建议](https://github.com/github/spec-kit/issues/new) · [贡献指南](./CONTRIBUTING.md) · [行为准则](./CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) Spec Kit 采用 [MIT 许可证](./LICENSE)。
